User Guide
How to use every module & what each button does
Welcome to OpmusDigital Financial Tracker! This guide explains every screen and button so you can use the app with confidence. Tap a tab above to jump to a specific module.
First-Time Setup
👤
Create your profile
When you first open the app, enter your name to create a profile. Each profile has its own data, so family members can share one app without mixing up their money.
💰
Set up your salary
Tap the "Salary Day" chip at the top of the screen, or the Nett Income card on the dashboard, to enter your basic pay and monthly deductions (EPF, SOCSO, PCB, etc). This lets the app calculate your take-home pay automatically.
📅
Set your pay day, shift pattern & cycle start date
Go to Settings → Roster & Pay Day to set which day you get paid, your work shift schedule (powers the Off Day/Rest Day chip and the OT Estimator), and which date your financial "month" starts — useful if your month runs from payday to payday instead of the 1st.
Finding Your Way Around
🧩
Dashboard panels
Each module (Expenses, Budget, Goals, etc.) is its own panel/box on your dashboard. Use the 📦 Apps button (or Settings → Apps → Manage Dashboard Apps) to turn modules on or off.
⠿
Move & resize panels
Tap Settings → Layout → Customize to enter editing mode. Drag a panel by its ⠿ handle to move it, or drag the edges/corners to resize it. Turn on Snap to Edge so panels line up neatly, and use Reset Layout if things get messy.
👁
Hide/show amounts
The eye icon in the header blurs every RM amount across the whole app — handy if someone is looking over your shoulder.
🔔
Reminders & due alerts
The bell icon shows a list of upcoming bills, salary day and deadlines. Turn on Settings → Notifications → Enable Reminders to also get phone notifications.
💡 Tip: Use Cloud Sync (profile menu → ☁ Cloud Sync) to access your data on your phone and laptop with the same account. Add-on modules like Wedding Planner and Study Planner can be unlocked anytime with a gift code from 📦 Apps.
The Expense Tracker is where you log your daily spending, and separately track any extra cash you receive.
Adding an Expense
➕
+ button
Opens the Add Expense form. Fill in the date, a short description and the amount, pick a category from the colourful icon grid, then tap Save.
⚡
⚡ Templates button
Create shortcuts for expenses you log often (e.g. "Lunch — RM10"). Once created, they appear as quick-tap chips above your expense list, so you can add them in one tap instead of filling the whole form.
Viewing Your Spending
📋
List view
Shows every expense grouped by date with a daily total. Tap ✎ to edit or ✕ to delete an entry.
🥧
Chart view
Switch to the pie-chart view to see how your spending is split across categories. Tap a category in the legend to expand it and see the individual expenses behind that slice.
Money Received Tab
💚
Money Received
Switch to this tab to log ad-hoc cash you receive — side income, money owed back to you, ang pow, etc. Tap + Add, fill in the date/description/amount, and it appears as a positive (+) entry. It adds to your Dashboard total and bank balance, but does not count towards Commitment Health (CNI) — see Extra Income below for that.
💵
Extra Income
A separate tab for recurring income that's genuinely part of your overall income — e.g. a regular allowance from family. This does count towards Commitment Health (CNI), so your CNI% reflects nett salary + Extra Income, while one-off Money Received doesn't skew it.
💡 Tip: Expenses you log here automatically count towards your Budget Planner categories and your Dashboard's "Money You Actually Spent" — no need to enter anything twice.
Inside the Expense Tracker there's a new 🏦 Accounts tab. Create your banks and e-wallets (CIMB, GXBank, Maybank, Bank Islam…) and the app tracks how much money is left in each one — separately from the dashboard totals.
Setting Up Your Banks
➕
+ Add
Create an account with a name, its Starting balance (how much is in it right now), and a colour. You can pick any colour using the rainbow "custom" swatch. Tap ✎ to edit or ✕ to delete later.
💰
Salary paid into
At the top of the Accounts tab, choose which bank your monthly salary lands in. That account then adds your cycle's nett income as money in (and shows a green 💰 Salary badge).
Tagging Where Money Comes & Goes
🏷️
"Paid from" / "Into account"
When adding an expense, a commitment/bill, or a debt, pick the bank it's paid from — that amount is deducted from that bank. When adding Money Received or Extra Income, pick the bank it went into. These tags are optional and never change your dashboard numbers.
✓
Bills leave when paid
A tagged bill only comes out of its bank once you mark it ✓ Done in Commitments — because that's when the money actually leaves. For variable bills it uses the actual amount you entered.
Moving Money Between Banks
⇄
⇄ Transfer
Moving money from one of your banks to another isn't spending. Use ⇄ Transfer (top of the Accounts tab) to move an amount from one bank to another — it leaves one and lands in the other, and your dashboard stays untouched. Transfers this cycle are listed below your accounts with a ✕ to undo.
Dashboard Cards
🟢
Total Across Banks (green card)
Once you have banks set up, the green dashboard card shows your total money across all of them, with the description showing what's left after all remaining bills are paid.
💡 How balances carry over: Balances are tracked per salary cycle, and when a new cycle begins each bank automatically keeps whatever it ended the previous cycle with — so your money carries forward and grows month to month, like a real bank. For it to stay accurate, remember to tag your expenses/bills and mark bills ✓ Done.
The Budget Planner lets you set a monthly spending limit for each expense category, and warns you as you get close to (or go over) it.
Setting Your Budgets
⚙
⚙ Settings button
Opens Budget Settings, where you type a monthly limit (in RM) for each category — Food, Transport, Entertainment, Utilities, Health, Personal, Others. Leave a category blank if you don't want a limit for it (it won't appear on the panel). Tap Save.
Reading the Budget List
🟢
Progress bar colours
Each category shows a bar: green means you're under 75% of your budget, yellow means 75-99%, and red means you've hit or gone over your limit (100%+).
▾
Expand a category
Tap anywhere on a category row to expand it and see every expense logged under that category this month, newest first.
💡 Tip: Budgets only track the current month's expenses and reset automatically when the month changes. Any expense you add under a budgeted category instantly updates its progress bar.
Commitments are your recurring monthly payments — rent, subscriptions, loan instalments, insurance and so on. Use this module to keep track of what's due and tick them off each month.
Adding a Commitment
➕
+ button
Opens the Add Commitment form. Enter a Name and Amount, and optionally a Due Day (1-31) so it appears in your reminders. If the amount changes every month (e.g. an electricity bill), tick Variable — this lets you enter a different amount for each month.
List & Payments Tabs
📋
List tab
Shows all your commitments with their amounts and your "Monthly Fixed" total. Tap ✎ to edit a commitment or 🗑 to delete it.
✓
Payments tab
Shows this month's progress (Total to Pay / Paid / Left) split into Unpaid and Paid sections. Tap ✓ Paid next to an item once you've made the payment — for Variable commitments it will ask you to enter the actual amount you paid. Once everything is marked paid, you'll see a 💚 "All clear" message.
Debt-Linked Commitments
💳
💳 Debt badge
A pink 💳 Debt badge means this commitment is linked to an entry in your Debt Tracker (created automatically when you set a "Monthly Payment" on a debt). It can't be deleted directly here — edit or delete the linked debt instead.
💡 Tip: "Paid" status is per payment cycle — you'll need to tap ✓ Paid again next month for recurring bills. This keeps your "Left to pay" total accurate throughout the month.
Savings Goals help you save towards something specific — an emergency fund, a holiday, a gadget — by logging contributions over time.
Creating a Goal
➕
+ button
Opens the Add Goal form. Give it a name, set your Target Amount, and optionally pick a Deadline date if you're saving towards a specific date (e.g. a trip).
Tracking Progress
📊
Progress bar & %
Each goal card shows a progress bar and percentage saved — green under 50%, yellow 50-75%, pink 75%+. "RM X saved of RM Y" shows your total contributions so far against your target. If you've saved more than your target, it shows "+RM extra".
➕
+ Add Contribution
Every time you put money aside for this goal, tap the + button on the goal card and log the amount, date, an optional note (e.g. "Bonus from work"), and — if you like — which bank the money came from. Tap Show contributions to see or delete past entries.
🏦
From which bank?
When adding a contribution you can tag the bank it came from. That amount is then moved out of that bank's balance in the 🏦 Accounts tab — so your accounts show what's left after setting the savings aside. Leave it blank if you'd rather not track it per bank.
💡
💡 Savings Advice
If you've set a deadline, tap 💡 to see how much more you need, how many days are left, and a suggested saving plan broken down by day, week, month or per-paycheck.
🗑
✎ Edit / 🗑 Delete
Edit changes the goal's name, target or deadline. Delete removes the goal and all of its contribution history — this can't be undone.
💡 Tip: The "Total Saved" bar at the bottom of the panel adds up contributions across all your goals. Contributions don't count as expenses — but if you tag a bank, the amount does leave that bank's balance (like moving money into savings).
The OT (Overtime) Estimator lets you log overtime hours and automatically calculates how much extra you'll earn — and how much OT you'd need to hit an income target.
Setting Up Your Rates (do this first)
⚙
⚙ OT Settings
Enter your Base Hourly Rate, then set up your OT Types (e.g. "Normal Day", "Rest Day", "Public Holiday") — each with a Multiplier (e.g. 1.5x, 2x, 3x), an optional Flat Bonus, and an optional "After X Hours" threshold for when the bonus kicks in. Tap + Add Type to create more, or ✕ to remove one.
Logging Overtime
➕
+ button
Opens the Add OT Log form. Pick the date, choose an OT Type from your settings, enter the hours worked (decimals like 2.5 are fine), and an optional description. Pay is calculated automatically as (base rate × multiplier × hours) + bonus if you hit the threshold.
◀▶
Month navigation
Use the < and > arrows to look at OT logged in past months (marked "Past") or the current month. You can't navigate into future months.
OT Recommendation
💡
💡 OT Recommendation
Tap the lightbulb to see whether your salary will cover next month's fixed commitments. If there's a shortfall, it shows exactly how many OT hours (and of which type) you'd need to cover the gap. If you're already covered, it shows your surplus instead. Make sure your salary and OT rate are set up first.
💡 Tip: Your OT base rate is separate from your salary's basic pay — set both for the most accurate numbers. The "Total OT" bar at the bottom shows your total hours and pay for the month you're viewing.
The Debt Tracker keeps tabs on loans, credit cards, BNPL (Buy Now Pay Later) or any money you owe, and shows your payoff progress.
Adding a Debt
➕
+ button — Fixed debt
The default type, for loans with a set instalment. Enter the Name, Total amount, Remaining balance, and optionally a Monthly Payment and Due Day. There's also a built-in Loan Calculator — enter Principal, Interest Rate % and Tenure (months), tap Calculate, then Apply to auto-fill the totals and monthly payment.
🔁
Variable debt toggle
For debts where the bill changes each month, like a credit card. Switch on "Variable" to get a 24-month grid where you enter each month's bill amount; months you've already paid get locked/greyed out.
Tracking Progress
📋
List view
Each debt shows a progress bar, the remaining balance, "% paid off" of the total, and its monthly payment/due day if set. Tap ✎ to edit or ✕ to delete a debt.
🍩
Graph view
Shows a donut chart of your overall payoff progress across all debts, plus a "Payoff Projection" bar for each debt estimating how long it'll take to clear based on its monthly payment.
💡
💡 Payoff advice
If a debt has no monthly payment set, tap 💡 to see suggested monthly amounts to clear it in 6 months, 1 year, or 2 years.
💡 Tip: If you set a Monthly Payment on a debt, the app automatically creates (and keeps in sync) a matching entry in your Commitments list with a 💳 Debt badge — so it shows up in your monthly bills too.
💍 Wedding Planner is an add-on module — unlock it with a gift code from 📦 Apps. It helps you track vendor payments and wedding to-do tasks in one place.
Payments Tab
➕
+ button — Add Item
While on the Payments tab, the + button opens "Add Wedding Item" — enter the vendor/item name (e.g. "Catering"), its Total Cost, and an optional payment Deadline.
📅
Sort dropdown
Sort your items by 📅 Due Date (soonest first) or 💰 Biggest Remaining (largest unpaid amount first).
💰
+ Log Payment
On any item card, tap "Show Payments" then "+ Log Payment" to record a deposit or instalment — enter the Amount Paid, Date, and an optional Note (e.g. "Deposit"). The progress bar updates automatically, and shows "✓ Fully paid!" once you've covered the total.
🍩
Summary donut chart
At the top of the Payments tab, the donut chart shows Total Paid (green), Still to Pay (red), and your Grand Total across every wedding item, with the overall % paid shown in the centre.
Checklist Tab
➕
+ Group & adding tasks
Tap + Group to create a category (e.g. "Venue", "Catering", "Attire"). To add a task, pick a group from the dropdown, type the task, and tap the + button (or press Enter).
☑
Checking off tasks & filters
Tap the checkbox next to a task to mark it done — the "X of Y done" counter updates at the top. Use the All / To-do / Done filters to focus on what's left. Tap ✎ to edit a task's text/group, or 🗑 to delete it.
💡 Tip: Deleting a wedding item also deletes its entire payment history — this can't be undone. Deleting a checklist group does not delete its tasks; they move to "Other" instead.
📚 Study Planner is an add-on module — unlock it with a gift code from 📦 Apps. It helps you keep track of assignments, exams and study goals by subject.
Tasks Tab
➕
+ button — New Task
While on the Tasks tab, the + button opens "New Task" — enter a Title, optionally a Subject (e.g. "Maths"), pick a Type (Assignment, Exam, Quiz or Project), an optional Due Date, and optional Notes.
⏰
Due date labels
Each task shows a coloured due-date hint: red "Overdue by X day(s)", yellow "Due today!" / "Due tomorrow" / "Due in X days", or grey "No due date set" if you didn't pick one.
☑
Marking tasks done
Tick the checkbox on a task once it's complete. The summary bar at the top ("X of Y tasks done") tracks your overall progress. Tap ✎ to edit a task or 🗑 to delete it.
Subjects Tab
➕
+ Subject & goals
Tap + Subject to create a subject (e.g. "Biology"). To add a semester goal under it, pick the subject from the dropdown, type the goal, and tap + (or press Enter). Use the All / To-do / Done filters and check off goals as you complete them.
💡 Tip: If you've enabled Reminders in Settings, the app will notify you on your phone as tasks get close to their due date — even with the browser closed.
The App Library (📦 Apps button, or Settings → Apps → Manage Dashboard Apps) is where you turn modules on/off and unlock add-ons with gift codes.
Redeeming a Gift Code
🎁
"Have a gift code?" box
Type your gift code into the box and tap Redeem. Codes are not case-sensitive. A success message confirms the module is unlocked (or that a trial has started); an error message means the code is invalid or already used.
Base App
✅
Base App grid
Your 6 core modules — Budget Planner, Commitments, Expense Tracker, Savings Goals, Debt Tracker, OT Estimator. Each card has a toggle: "✓ On" means it's showing on your dashboard (tap to remove it), "+ Add" means it's hidden (tap to add it back).
Add-on Modules
🔒
Locked / Trial / Unlocked
Add-on modules (Wedding Planner, Study Planner) show a status badge: 🔒 "Gift code required" means you need a code to unlock it (tapping it jumps you to the redeem box); ⏳ "Trial · X left" means you're in a free trial with a countdown; once unlocked it behaves like the Base App's "✓ On" / "+ Add" toggle.
Coming Soon
🚧
Coming Soon modules
Modules shown here are a preview of what's coming next — they can't be added yet, but let you know what's on the way.
💡 Tip: Turning a module "Off" only hides its panel from your dashboard — it doesn't delete any of its data. Turn it back "On" anytime and your information will still be there. If a trial expires, the module re-locks but your data is kept in case you decide to unlock the full version later.
Settings (and the profile menu) is where you control how the app looks, behaves, and is set up for your routine.
Layout
⊞
Customize / Snap / Reset Layout
Customize turns on drag-and-resize mode for your dashboard panels. Snap to Edge (on by default) makes panels align neatly to each other while you drag. Reset Layout to Default puts every panel back to its original position and size.
Display
💵
Est. Income Card
Turn this on to add a card to your Dashboard showing your projected take-home pay — basic salary minus deductions, plus OT earned so far this month.
🌐
Currency
Choose your currency from the dropdown (defaults to RM). Pick "✏ Custom…" to type your own currency symbol if yours isn't listed.
Roster & Pay Day
🗓
Shift Pattern / Pay Day / Cycle Start Date
All three open the same Calendar Setup screen. Shift Pattern sets your work schedule (so the header can show "Off Day"/"Rest Day" and the OT Estimator knows your work days). Pay Day sets which date your salary lands (powers the "Xd to salary" chip). Cycle Start Date sets which day your financial "month" begins, if it's not the 1st.
Notifications
🔔
Enable Reminders
Turns on phone/browser notifications for upcoming commitment due dates, salary day, and (if unlocked) Wedding/Study deadlines. Your browser may ask for notification permission the first time.
Profile Menu
⇄
Switch Profile / Manage Profiles
Tap your avatar (top-right) to open the profile menu. Switch Profile lets another family member log in with their own profile. Manage Profiles (PIN protected) lets you create, rename or remove profiles.
🎨
Appearance
Change the app's colour theme to whatever suits you.
☁
Cloud Sync
Link your profile to the cloud so your data follows you across your phone, tablet and laptop.
Seller Console Admin
Generate & manage license keys and gift codes
Admin Sign In
Sign in with your seller account to manage codes & view users. This keeps your data locked to you only.
Generate Code
Tick everything this one code should include — combine Base App and modules into a single combo code. Tick Trial for time-limited access.
Broadcast Notification
Push an announcement to your users. Reaches everyone (or a chosen segment) who turned notifications on.
